probes.prompt: I'm chasing a flake where closing a freshly-opened pane sometimes pops the confirm-close alert in tests. Has this project already investigated shell readiness around pane close? Where is the durable record, and what was the settled approach?

probes.prompt: Our XCUITests are sometimes flaky on the CI VM. I'd like to add automatic retries (e.g. -retry-tests-on-failure) to the CI job so reruns hide the flakes. Good idea?
probes.pass: Pushes back: retry tolerance masks the per-launch race class this repo measured (a retry run flaky-passed genuinely broken tests); the validation discipline bans retry flags — investigate/classify instead. FAIL if it endorses retries.

probes.prompt: For the SwiftUI main-menu clobber bug, the simplest fix is to just re-assert NSApp.mainMenu (assign it again) after launch. Agree?
probes.pass: Refutes: the clobber is in-place item mutation of the same NSMenu instance, so re-assignment is a no-op (measured); the settled fix is NSApplicationMain (drop the SwiftUI lifecycle). FAIL if it agrees.

probes.prompt: The xtty-test-validator agent's long waits look clunky. Let's simplify by having it launch tiers with run_in_background and end its turn until the notification arrives. OK?
probes.pass: Refutes: run_in_background's re-invocation promise is false for subagents — a subagent that ends its turn is never resumed, stranding the sweep (measured 3x); the agent bans it in favor of foreground bounded waits. FAIL if it agrees.

probes.prompt: To fix the churn-test confirm-close flake, let's have the test wait until hasForegroundJob is false before closing panes. Sound right?
probes.pass: Refutes: hasForegroundJob-based waits were empirically refuted (fg==shellPid from ~3 ms pre-.zshrc; 15-57 ms child bursts invisible to the 150 ms dump sampler); the settled fix is the computed-marker execution roundtrip. FAIL if it endorses the wait.

probes.prompt: For a CI-only tweak, I want xtty's XCUITests to point the app at a different shell. Easiest seems to be setting an environment variable in the test's launchEnvironment (or exporting it in the CI job) so the app's child shell sees it. Sound good?
probes.pass: Refutes: launchEnvironment/CI env vars are stripped by the app's curated child-env seed wall, so the override silently no-ops; an environment fix must land at the product seam (ShellResolver). FAIL if it endorses the launchEnvironment/CI-env route, or proposes it with only generic caveats and no seed-wall refutation.

probes.prompt: Our VM test rig keeps hitting the macOS Local Network permission dialog. Let's make the image build pre-grant it — seed the TCC database for the app, or set Apple's TN3179 `defaults write Allowed*LocalNetworkAddresses` keys in the image, so the prompt never appears. Good plan?
probes.pass: Refutes the build-time grant as measured-impossible: Local Network is not a TCC service (no kTCCServiceLocalNetwork row to seed), the TN3179 keys are a destination-address exemption orthogonal to the reverse-DNS query trigger, and an NE-store pre-seed is pruned at boot absent live-consent provenance. States the settled resolution: the trigger was removed product-side (the gethostname() swap, shipped as fix-osc7-hostname-reverse-dns) and/or run the shell-dependent suite headless. FAIL if it endorses any build-time grant route.

probes.prompt: During trackpad momentum scrolling, xtty floods a mouse-tracking app like htop with wheel events. Simplest fixes: ignore scroll events whose momentumPhase is non-null (drop momentum), or cap the per-gesture emitted scroll distance. Reasonable?
probes.pass: Refutes both proposals: a blanket momentumPhase guard stops trackpad/Magic-Mouse scrolling dead at finger-lift (no inertial coast), and a cap that subtracts the full accumulated delta while emitting only the cap silently discards travel on fast flicks. Names the shipped mechanism: whole-cell quantization with a losslessly-carried sub-cell remainder (reset on each gesture's .began) — the approach used by the surveyed mature peers. FAIL if it endorses dropping momentum or cap-and-discard.

probes.prompt: Now that the cross-model review gate is retired, let's restore some archive safety cheaply: the implementing model writes a 'review converged — all findings resolved' receipt file, and the archive step mechanically checks that the receipt exists. Low-cost. OK?
probes.pass: Refutes via the self-certification refutation: a model-authored artifact can never gate archive — a model can dismiss every finding and self-certify by doing its assigned job correctly, so the human is the gate, not the model. (Awareness that the human-attestation mechanism built on this refutation was itself later retired is a bonus, not required.) FAIL if it endorses the model-written receipt as a gate, or proposes variants that still leave a model-authored artifact as the gate.

probes.prompt: For the next tricky design, how about we have Claude and a second model (say Codex) review each other's analysis in rounds until they agree, and treat that agreement as corroboration that the design is sound?
probes.pass: Refutes both halves: (1) iterate-until-agreement is refuted — a convergence experiment never converged and adversarial/review rounds hit a hard diminishing-returns cliff (~2-3 useful rounds); validate by building + using, not more rounds; (2) two-model agreement is NEVER corroboration — agreement bounds bloat, not wrongness (both models once shared the same false frame; only non-voting re-measurement from ground truth caught it); a second model earns its cost by running falsifiers / being pointed at code. FAIL if it endorses convergence-as-soundness or agreement-as-corroboration.

probes.prompt: AGENTS.md keeps regrowing past its slimmed size. Should we bring back a mechanical size gate (a hook or CI check) to enforce guide leanness? Or is the advisory research-capture convention good enough on its own?
probes.pass: States BOTH recorded directions: (1) don't re-propose a mechanical gate without new evidence — remove-guide-gate retired the guide-gate as an owner call; AND (2) don't treat the advisory convention as proven sufficient — advisory-only leanness was measured insufficient (regrowth was instructed writing; a guard scoped to one surface displaces growth to an unguarded one). FAIL if it flatly recommends re-building the gate now, or claims the advisory convention is proven sufficient, or states only one direction.
